title: Check the pairs, like ImGui's asserts
description:
ImGui asserts when `Begin`/`End` and `PushID`/`PopID` calls do not pair up. Write a checker that reports the first mistake in one frame's calls:

```cpp
struct Call { std::string name; bool result{ true }; };   // result: what a Begin... function returned

std::string checkFrame(const std::vector<Call>& calls);
```

The calls are `Begin`, `End`, `BeginChild`, `EndChild`, `BeginTable`, `EndTable`, `BeginMenu`, `EndMenu`, `PushID` and `PopID`. The rules:

- `Begin` and `BeginChild`: the matching `End`/`EndChild` is **always** required, whatever they returned.
- `BeginTable` and `BeginMenu`: the matching end is required **only if** it returned `true`, and must **not** be called if it returned `false`.
- `PushID` needs a `PopID` before the scope it was pushed in ends.
- Ends must match the most recent open thing: `EndTable` when the innermost open item is a `Begin` window is wrong.

Return the first problem as one of these messages (with the call's position `i`, counting from 0):

- `"<End...> at <i> has no matching <Begin...>"`: an end with nothing matching open, or that does not match the innermost open item;
- `"<End...> at <i> was called although <Begin...> returned false"`: ending a `BeginTable`/`BeginMenu` that returned false (when its end would be the next end of that type);
- `"missing <End...> for <Begin...> at <i>"`: the frame ended while something was still open (report the innermost one, with the position of its begin).

Return `""` when everything pairs up.
hints: Keep a stack of open items. A `BeginTable` or `BeginMenu` that returned `false` is not pushed: remember it separately, so a stray `EndTable` can be reported with the better message.
lessonTitle: The Demo Window and the Debug Tools
